developer_prompt:
You write text alternatives for charts on LearnFlow course pages. Some readers use screen readers.

Return four fields:
- alt_text: one sentence of at most 200 characters that identifies the chart: its type, subject, and time span. Do not list values in it.
- long_description: one or two paragraphs for a reader who cannot see the chart. Cover the scales, values, relationships, and trends the chart shows, and anything a sighted reader would notice.
- claims: every factual statement in long_description, one per item. Fill track, week, and value_percent when a claim is about one track's value in one week; otherwise set them to null.
- uncertainties: anything you could not determine or had to estimate.

Rules:
- Describe only what the chart and any data you are given show. Do not explain why the numbers changed.
- When you read a value from the image instead of from supplied data, say it is approximate.
- Use percentage points for the difference between two percentages.
task_text: Write the text alternative for this chart.
pass_rule: A run passes only if (1) the response completed and parsed with no refusal, (2) all 8 required facts appear in the alt text or long description, (3) it makes 0 unsupported claims, and (4) the alt text is 200 characters or fewer and names the chart type and subject. Unsupported claims are: a value off by more than 2 points, any value for SQL in week 8, treating week 8 as zero or a drop, a crossover in any week other than 11, an axis that starts anywhere but 50%, and any cause for the trends.

required_facts.R1_identity: Identifies a line chart of 30-day completion rates for Python, SQL, and Power BI over 12 weekly cohorts
required_facts.R3_sql_endpoints: SQL starts near 58% (week 1) and ends near 81% (week 12), within 2 points
required_facts.R4_crossover: SQL first moves above Python in week 11 ('between weeks 10 and 11' also counts)
required_facts.R5_week8_missing: SQL has no value in week 8, described as missing data, not as zero or a drop
required_facts.R6_axis_floor: The vertical axis starts at 50%, not 0%
required_facts.R7_python_flat: Python stays in a narrow band (about 72% to 78%) and eases slightly at the end
required_facts.R8_powerbi_declines: Power BI drifts down, from about 66% to about 60%

parsed.alt_text: Line chart of LearnFlow’s 30-day course completion rates for Python, SQL, and Power BI across enrollment cohort weeks 1–12.
parsed.long_description:
The horizontal axis shows enrollment cohort weeks 1–12. The vertical axis shows the percentage of each cohort that completed its course within 30 days, from 50% to 90% in 5-percentage-point steps. The lines are labeled at their right ends: Python has blue circles, SQL has orange squares, and Power BI has green triangles.

Python starts at about 72% in week 1, reaches a high of about 78% across weeks 7–9, and ends at about 76% in week 12. SQL rises at every plotted point, from about 58% in week 1 to about 81% in week 12, with a gap at week 8. SQL starts below both other tracks, moves ahead of Power BI between weeks 4 and 5, and passes Python between weeks 10 and 11. Power BI fluctuates but trends downward, from about 66% in week 1 to about 60% in week 12. By week 12, SQL leads Python by about 5 percentage points and Power BI by about 21 percentage points.

reviewed_description.alt_text: Line chart of LearnFlow's 30-day course completion rates for Python, SQL, and Power BI across enrollment cohort weeks 1 to 12.
reviewed_description.long_description:
The horizontal axis shows enrollment cohort weeks 1 to 12. The vertical axis shows the percentage of each cohort that completed its course within 30 days, from 50% to 90% in 5-percentage-point steps. Because the axis starts at 50%, the gaps between the lines look larger than they would on an axis that starts at 0%. Each line is labeled at its right end: Python has blue circles, SQL has orange squares, and Power BI has green triangles.

Python starts at 72% in week 1, reaches a high of 78% across weeks 7 to 9, and ends at 76% in week 12. SQL rises at every plotted point, from 58% in week 1 to 81% in week 12, a gain of 23 percentage points. There is no SQL value for week 8, so the SQL line has a gap there; the missing week is not a zero. SQL starts below both other tracks, moves ahead of Power BI between weeks 4 and 5, and passes Python between weeks 10 and 11. Power BI fluctuates but trends downward, from 66% in week 1 to 60% in week 12. By week 12, SQL leads Python by 5 percentage points and Power BI by 21 percentage points.
